where: Appendix D.4 (90-appendices.md lines 210-231) vs §11.2 (10-cli-contract.md lines 236-340). Examples: D.4 'AccountEntry ... {name, kind, label?, state..., reason?, enabled, usageProbe, ...}'; D.4 '`list <cli>`: {contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, accounts:[AccountEntry]}'; D.4 '`status [cli]`: ... plus top-level vault:{...} and agySlot?:{owner?, ...}'; D.4 'accounts:[{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}]'; D.4 'recorded ... {account, class, kind?, scope?, until?, untilEpoch?, tier?, limitSource?, resetConfidence?, limitType?}'; D.4 '`next`: ... `switched` = (`account` ≠ `previous`)'; D.4 'Status file (`exec` / `run --status-file PATH` ...) postRunError?:{code, reason?}' vs §11.2 line 340 '`postRunError`: `null`, or `{code, message}`'
problem: D.4 now has field lists, but they disagree with §11.2, and §18.2 asserts every §11 response against the D schemas. (1) §11.2 list entries carry `id` (line 238, 249), but D.4 AccountEntry has none. (2) The §11.2 list object carries `poolDropped`, but D.4 `list` omits it. (3) §11.2 puts `agySlot` in the agy per-cli object and defines top-level `notice:{accepted, version, acceptedAt, acceptedAtEpoch}`, which §15.7 item 6 reads. It also adds relogin, attentionCode, authStrikes, lastStrikeAt, lastOkAt and utilization per status account entry. D.4 puts agySlot at the top level and has no notice and none of those account fields. (4) In pick/next, §11.2 accounts[] entries are {name, state, reason, limitedUntil, limitedUntilEpoch, limits}, but D.4 drops reason and limits. (5) §11.2 `recorded` has `relogin` and `attentionCode`, but D.4 lacks them. (6) D.4's switched=(account≠previous) makes a 69/77 next (account:null) switched:true, while §11.2 requires both to be non-null. (7) postRunError is {code, message} in §11.2 but {code, reason} in D.4 and §12.1.1. (8) D.4 names a `run --status-file`, but §10.4 lists --status-file for exec only and the §16 run syntax has no such flag.
fix: Make D.4 match §11.2 exactly: add `id` to AccountEntry; add `poolDropped:[name]` to the list per-cli object. Status: top-level `notice:{accepted, version?, acceptedAt?, acceptedAtEpoch?}`. Move `agySlot?:{owner?, store?, writtenAt?, writtenAtEpoch?, saveBackPending}` into the agy per-cli object. Add `relogin?:{reason, since, sinceEpoch}, attentionCode?, authStrikes, lastStrikeAt?, lastStrikeAtEpoch?, lastOkAt?, lastOkAtEpoch?, utilization?` to status account entries. Make pick/next/mark accounts[] `{name, state, reason?, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?, limits:[Limit]}`, and add `relogin?` and `attentionCode?` to `recorded`. next: 'switched is true when account and previous are both non-null and differ'. In §11.2 change postRunError to `{code, reason}`. In D.4 write 'Status file (`exec --status-file PATH`)', dropping `run`.

where: §15.3 v2 engine: "$launch = if ($acct) { Resolve-CliLaunch -Command $script:AccShiftBin -CliArgs (@('exec', $cli, '--account', $acct, '--status-file', $statusFile, '--') + @($inv.Args)) }" and "next <cli> --from $acct --model $model --limited-model $model ..."
problem: `$acct` now has a defined source (pick before each attempt), and the 75, auth-continue and preflight parts are in. But the v2 snippet introduces `$cli` and `$model`, which Invoke-CliRoleOnce never defines. They are locals of Get-CliInvocation (v2/lib/Cli.ps1:280-281); Invoke-CliRoleOnce has `$roleCfg.Cli` / `$roleCfg.Model`. v2 runs without StrictMode, so `$cli` is $null, or a same-named variable from a caller through PowerShell's dynamic scoping. Every routed v2 launch then becomes `accshift exec <nothing> --account ...` and fails with 125 `usage`/`unknown-cli`. This is the leaked/undefined-CLI-variable defect of CI#2 again, now in the v2 engine. §15.2's list of `<cli>` variables also omits v2.
fix: In §15.3 v2: use `([string]$roleCfg.Cli)` in place of `$cli` and `[string]$roleCfg.Model` in place of `$model` in the Resolve-CliLaunch snippet and in the pick/next/mark calls. Add 'v2: `$roleCfg.Cli`' to the `<cli>` variable list in §15.2.

where: §15.3 Types: "a rest is `Invoke-UiRestWithSummary -Cli $cli -WakeTime ([DateTimeOffset]::FromUnixTimeSeconds([long]$j.resetAtEpoch).LocalDateTime.AddMinutes($Settings.ResetBufferMinutes))`"
problem: The [datetime] conversion rule is in place. But the prescribed call runs in the ps1 run loops (single-runner and fallbacks pick and limit hooks), where neither `$cli` nor `$Settings` exists. v1 limitshift.ps1 runs the loop at script scope with `$task`, `$activeRunner`, `$config.Settings` and `$ResetBufferMinutes` (:3066, :3299 `Wait-ForLimitReset ... -Settings $config.Settings`). `$Settings` is only a parameter of Wait-ForLimitReset / Wait-ForRunnerReset, and `$cli` is a local of Read-QueueConfig's Parse-Runner (:983). Under `Set-StrictMode -Version 2.0` (:13) both references throw, which is the crash CI#14 was about. The call also uses a bare `$cli`, contrary to §15.2's 'never a leftover global'.
fix: Replace it with `Invoke-UiRestWithSummary -Cli $task.Cli -WakeTime ([DateTimeOffset]::FromUnixTimeSeconds([long]$j.resetAtEpoch).LocalDateTime.AddMinutes($config.Settings.ResetBufferMinutes))`. Fallbacks use `$activeRunner.Cli`; v2-root roles use `$verifierTask.Cli` / `$plannerTask.Cli`. Add: 'the run loops have no `$Settings` or `$cli`; use `$config.Settings` and the launched runner's `.Cli`'.

where: §15.7 intro: "`--validate-only` calls only read-only commands (`version`, `list`, `status`, `pick`, `doctor --json`; §11.1 rule 8)." vs §15.5: "`agy models` and `--probe-models` run through `accshift exec agy --account X` ... agy discovery runs only for the live slot owner: `pick agy` without `--prefer` names it, and exec takes the shared fast path for it, which writes no slot" and §15.7 item 8
problem: The fix (discovery only for the live owner, never swap) is in place, but it contradicts §15.7's rule that validate-only calls only read-only commands. v1 discover_cli_models runs `agy models` during --validate-only, so validate-only now runs `exec agy`, which is a writer under §11.1 rule 8: save-back and agyBinary writes, and it takes the slot lock. It is also wrong that 'exec takes the shared fast path for it'. The shared path exists only once V-A8 has passed (§13.1, §8.3.3 A). Otherwise exec takes the exclusive path, which runs the foreign-process check: with the user's own agy open it fails 125 `agy-busy`, and it writes the vault save-back. No validate-only outcome is specified for that failure.
fix: Pick one rule and state it in both places. Either (a) §15.7: 'validate-only calls only read-only commands, plus, for agy model discovery, one `exec agy --account <live owner>` (§15.5), which never swaps; a 125 from it (for example `agy-busy`) is a WARNING and the cached capabilities are used', or (b) validate-only never runs exec and uses only the cached capabilities. In §15.5 replace 'exec takes the shared fast path for it' with 'exec takes the shared fast path once V-A8 has passed, else the exclusive path; either way the live owner's slot is not rewritten'.

where: §15.2 exec table: "| every other code; also 126 and 127 | needs-human, no retry |" vs §15.3 bash: "if [ \"$R_EXIT\" = 125 ] && [ \"$ACCT_LAUNCHED\" != true ]; then acct_outcome exec 125 \"$ACCT_ERR\"" and ps1 "the post-run hooks (125 check, then `wrongAccount` and `mark --ok`)"
problem: §15.2 makes exec's own 126 (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`) and 127 (`not-found`) needs-human. The normative bash and ps1 hooks test only for 125. An accshift 126/127 with launched:false therefore goes down the normal CLI error path (classify, then the retry budget) instead of needs-human, so the hooks and the table disagree.
fix: In §15.3 change the check to `case $R_EXIT in 125|126|127) [ "$ACCT_LAUNCHED" != true ] && { acct_outcome exec "$R_EXIT" "$ACCT_ERR"; ... } ;; esac`, and the ps1 bullet to '(125–127 check with launched false ...)'. In v2 the status-file read applies the same 125–127 table.

where: §10.3 row 125/126/127: "126: the cli was found but is not executable (`not-executable`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found"; Appendix E: "| 127 | cli not found | exec, run | needs-human |" vs §12.1.1: "**126:** ... `not-executable` ..., `cmd-shim-unsupported` (§12.4) or `wsl-windows-binary` (§12.2). **127:** the binary was not found: `not-found` (§12.2)."
problem: The exit-code summaries disagree with §12.1.1. §10.3 omits the 126 code `cmd-shim-unsupported` (defined in §12.4 and listed in Appendix E). Neither §10.3 nor Appendix E names the 127 `error.code` `not-found`, which the status file and the stderr line carry and which LimitShift's per-code fallback parses.
fix: §10.3: '126: ... (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found (`not-found`)'. Appendix E 127 row: 'cli not found: `not-found` (§12.2)'.

where: §11.2: "**`pick` / `next` / `mark --json`** (`next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0` at 10:40Z ...)" with "recorded":{..."tier":3,"limitSource":"structured","resetConfidence":"exact"...}
problem: Claude tier-3 evidence comes only from a stream-json `rate_limit_event` or the transcript's `rate_limit_info` (§8.1 Limits, §9.4 tier table). LimitShift's `--output-format json` evidence file carries neither (D8 reason 5). Without `--session`/`--cwd` there is no transcript lookup, so the example call cannot produce the tier-3 `structured` record it shows. §5.2 passes `--session U --cwd D` for exactly this reason, and §6.3 stores the same record.
fix: Change the example invocation to `next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0 --session U --cwd D` (matching §5.2 and §15.2 step 2). Alternatively, show `"tier":2,"limitSource":"text","resetConfidence":"parsed"` and update the 75 example and §6.3 to match.

where: §15.7 item 4: "An `experimental` CLI → WARNING when the runner lists `accounts` (rotation unverified on this OS), else INFO \"not routed (experimental)\"; ERROR under `required` without `accounts` (§15.4)." and §15.4 `required` bullet: "if `experimental`, the runner must list `accounts` (otherwise a validate-only ERROR, and needs-human at run time)" vs §15.4 agy bullet: "an agy runner without `accounts` counts as listing every agy account, so it is routed even when agy is `experimental`" and acct_decide: "1 ... when the cli is agy with agy accounts registered"
problem: agy is `experimental` on every OS until its V-A items pass (§8.3.5, §11.2 example). While agy accounts are registered, an agy runner without `accounts` is routed (§15.4 agy rule, §15.3 acct_decide), under both auto and required. §15.7 item 4 prints INFO 'not routed (experimental)' for it under auto, and an ERROR (with needs-human at run time per the §15.4 required bullet) under required. Validate-only and the required rule therefore contradict the routing rule.
fix: In the §15.4 `required` bullet and §15.7 item 4, add: 'an agy runner while agy accounts are registered counts as listing `accounts` (§15.4 agy rule): it is routed, and validate-only prints a WARNING (rotation unverified on this OS), never INFO "not routed" or ERROR'.

where: Appendix D.4 `version`: "`stderrCatalogue` lists every stderr line template (§12.1.1)"
problem: §12.1.1 and §11.2 say catalogue messages interpolate nothing, and that `stderrCatalogue` lists every line verbatim, which is what makes it exhaustive for LimitShift's regex test (CI#6). Calling the entries 'templates' implies placeholders, which contradicts the no-interpolation rule an implementer would build the schema and the testdata file from.
fix: D.4: '`stderrCatalogue` lists, verbatim, every line `exec` can write to stderr; lines contain no placeholders or digits (§12.1.1)'.

where: Appendix D.4, pick/next/mark shape: "`{contract, cli, account?, previous?, switched, …, recorded?, accounts:[{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}], error?}`"
problem: SC#13 and decisions §5 require `list`/`status`/`accounts[]` to carry `limits:[…]`. §9.1 says "`list`, `status` and `accounts[]` report every active record as `limits:[…]`", and §11.2 says "Each entry is `{name, state, reason, limitedUntil, limitedUntilEpoch, limits}`". The §11.2 next and 75 examples print `reason` and `limits` in each accounts[] entry. D.4 is the normative schema that §18.2 validates every response against, and its accounts[] entry has neither `limits` nor `reason`. So a caller cannot see concurrent per-scope records in pick/next/mark responses, and the §11.2 examples fail the D.4 schema.
fix: In D.4 pick/next/mark, change the accounts[] element to `{name, state, reason?, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?, limits:[Limit]}`, with `Limit` as defined in D.4. State that `limits` lists every active record and that the summary fields follow the AccountEntry rule.

where: §11.2 heading of the pick/next/mark example: "(`next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0` at 10:40Z …)", whose output records `"tier":3,"limitSource":"structured"`. §11.3 bash recipe `"$ACCSHIFT" next claude --from "$acct" --model "$next_model" --limited-model "$model" --evidence-file … --run-started-at "$run_start" ${pool:+…} ${parsed_reset:+…} --json` and the PowerShell `$acctArgs = @('next', 'claude', …)`
problem: SC#17's FIX requires every next call to pass `--session`/`--cwd` for claude and codex, and §15.2 step 2 does. The §11.3 claude recipes, which callers copy, omit both flags. §10.4 says that without `--cwd` there is "no Claude transcript lookup". D8 reason 5 says LimitShift's `--output-format json` carries no `rate_limit_event`, so for LimitShift output claude tier 3 can come only from the transcript. The §11.2 example call therefore cannot produce the tier-3 `structured` record it shows. §5.2 runs the same scenario and passes `--session U --cwd D` for exactly this reason.
fix: Add `--session U --cwd D` to the §11.2 example call. In §11.3 add `${sid:+--session "$sid" --cwd "$project_path"}` to the bash recipe and `if ($sid) { $acctArgs += @('--session', $sid, '--cwd', $projectPath) }` to the PowerShell recipe, with the note "claude and codex only (§15.2)".

where: §9.4: "Pruning removes expired records but keeps a backoff entry until 24 h after its `lastHitAt`" and "Counters (`hits`, `rehitMinutes`, `authStrikes`) reset on `mark --ok`, or after 24 h without a new hit or strike". §9.2: "backoff entries 24 h after their `lastHitAt`". §6.3: "Pruning keeps an entry until 24 h after its `lastHitAt`". Early re-hit: "a limit hit while `lastUntil ≤ now < lastUntil + 15 min`"
problem: The early re-hit rule needs `lastUntil`, but the entry that holds it is deleted 24 h after the hit. For any record that lasts more than about 24 h (Claude `seven_day_opus`/`seven_day_sonnet`, Copilot weekly or monthly quotas), the entry is pruned before the record expires. The first re-hit after such a record therefore never gets the early re-hit backoff, which is the gap SC#11 was meant to close. The §6.3 example shows it: the `model:opus` entry has lastHitAt 1791368400 and lastUntil 1791784800, so it is pruned at 1791454800, about 3.8 days before lastUntil. The data-vault editor flagged this and left it open.
fix: Replace the retention rule in all three places with: "A backoff entry is kept until max(`lastHitAt` + 24 h, `lastUntil` + 15 min)". In §9.4 change the counter sentence to "`hits` and `rehitMinutes` reset on `mark --ok`, or when their entry is pruned; `authStrikes` after 24 h without a new strike". Add an §18.1 engine case: a 7-day record expires, and a hit within 15 minutes afterwards applies the early re-hit backoff.

where: §6.3 example, `claude/3f9a01c2`: `"lastOkAt": 1791369000` (10:30Z) together with `"model:opus": { "hits": 0, "lastUntil": 1791784800, "lastHitAt": 1791368400, "rehitMinutes": 0 }` (lastHitAt 10:20Z) in a snapshot taken at 10:45Z
problem: §6.3 says `lastOkAt` is written only by `mark --ok`, and §6.3, §9.2 and §9.4 say "`mark --ok` and `mark --clear` delete the whole map". The `mark --ok` at 10:30Z would have deleted the 10:20Z `model:opus` backoff entry, so the 10:45Z snapshot cannot contain it. The example contradicts the rule it documents, and §18.1's example-pair test would copy it into goldens. The scenario also exposes a rule gap: a successful Sonnet run wipes the backoff memory of a still-active Opus scope.
fix: Set `lastOkAt` to a time before the Opus hit, for example 1791367800 (2026-10-07T10:10:00Z), so that the story reads ok at 10:10, Opus limit at 10:20, five-hour limit at 10:40. Optional normative refinement: in §9.2/§9.4/§6.3, "`mark --ok` deletes the backoff entries of scopes that have no active record".

where: §6.3: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok`, a same-identity `login` and `mark --clear` clear them." and "A same-identity `login` clears `relogin`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt` and auth-suspect records". Compare §9.2 Success: mark --ok "keeps limit records, `relogin`, `attentionCode` and `lastStrikeAt` (the incident window of other accounts still sees that strike)". §9.2 Login effects and §8 Login rules: "clears `relogin`, `authStrikes` and auth-suspect records" (no lastStrikeAt)
problem: Two sections disagree on what `mark --ok` and a same-identity `login` clear. The §9.2 incident rule (step 2) counts accounts by `lastStrikeAt` within `authSuspectMinutes`. If `mark --ok` cleared it, as §6.3 says, a success on one account would hide that account's strike, and a provider outage could escalate the other accounts instead of being treated as an incident (SC#16).
fix: §6.3: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok` and a same-identity `login` clear `authStrikes` and keep `lastStrikeAt` (the incident window, §9.2); `mark --clear` and `login --new-identity` clear both." Remove `lastStrikeAt` from the same-identity login sentence in §6.3.

where: Appendix D.4: AccountEntry "`{name, kind, label?, state…}`"; "**`list <cli>`:** `{contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, accounts:[AccountEntry]}`"; "**`status [cli]`:** the `list` shape, plus top-level `vault:{…}` … and `agySlot?:{…}`… An agy AccountEntry in `status` adds `wrongAccount?…`"; "`recorded`: … `{account, class, kind?, scope?, until?, untilEpoch?, tier?, limitSource?, resetConfidence?, limitType?}`"; "`next`: … `switched` = (`account` ≠ `previous`)"; "**Status file** (`exec` / `run --status-file PATH`…)"
problem: D.4 is the schema that §18.2 validates every response against, and it no longer matches §11.2. (1) §11.2 list entries carry `id` ("An account entry has: `name`, `id` …"), but D.4 AccountEntry has none. (2) The §11.2 list example has `poolDropped`, which D.4 `list` lacks. (3) §11.2 `recorded` has `relogin` and `attentionCode`, which D.4 lacks. (4) §11.2 status adds top-level `notice:{accepted, version, acceptedAt, acceptedAtEpoch}`, puts `agySlot` in the agy per-cli object, and adds per-account `relogin`, `attentionCode`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt`, `lastOkAt` and `utilization`. D.4 has none of these, and places agySlot at the top level. §15.7 item 6 depends on `status --json` → `notice.accepted`. (5) D.4's `switched` = (account ≠ previous) makes 69/77 (account null) switched:true, while §11.2 requires both to be non-null. (6) D.4 gives `run` a `--status-file`, but §10.4 lists it for `exec` only and §16's run syntax has no such flag.
fix: Align D.4 with §11.2. AccountEntry gains `id`. `list <cli>` gains `poolDropped:[name]`. `recorded` gains `relogin?` and `attentionCode?`. `status` gains top-level `notice:{accepted, version?, acceptedAt?, acceptedAtEpoch?}`, `agySlot?` moves into the agy per-cli object, and every status AccountEntry adds `relogin?:{reason, since, sinceEpoch}`, `attentionCode?`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt?`/`lastStrikeAtEpoch?`, `lastOkAt?`/`lastOkAtEpoch?` and `utilization?`. Change `switched` to "true when `account` and `previous` are both non-null and differ". Change the status-file heading to "`exec --status-file PATH`", or add `--status-file` to `run` in §10.4 and §16.

where: §11.2 exec `--status-file`: "`postRunError`: `null`, or `{code, message}` when a post-run hook failed."
problem: §12.1.1 says "`postRunError`: null, or `{code, reason}`" and D.4 says `postRunError?:{code, reason?}`, so the field shape disagrees between sections. §12.1.1 also says the status file's shape "is in §11.2". The exec editor flagged this in round 2 and it is still unfixed.
fix: In §11.2 change it to "`postRunError`: `null`, or `{code, reason}` (for example `save-back-failed`, `copy-back-conflict`, `copy-back-skipped`, `copy-back-failed`, `agy-slot-unregistered`) when a post-run hook failed or was skipped."

where: §10.3: "126: the cli was found but is not executable (`not-executable`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found". Appendix E row 127: "cli not found"
problem: §12.1.1 defines 126 as `not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported` (§12.4) or `wsl-windows-binary`, and 127 as `not-found` (also §12.2). Appendix E's 126 row lists `cmd-shim-unsupported`, but §10.3 omits it. Neither §10.3 nor Appendix E names the 127 `error.code`.
fix: §10.3: "126: … (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found (`not-found`)". Appendix E row 127: "cli not found: `not-found` (§12.2)".

where: §15.2 'On a usage limit' step 3: "**0** → account B becomes the current account. Same CLI, model index 0, no sleep, and the session rule below. A codex refresh race can return B with `recorded.class:"transient"` ... it is handled the same way."
problem: §8.5, C.5 and §9.4 now classify Copilot `session_quota_exceeded` as class `error`, `rotate:false`, with the rule "The caller starts a new session". LimitShift is that caller, and §15 never applies the rule. LimitShift's own copilot limit regex contains `quota`, and R06 §3 notes it also matches the raw `"errorType":"quota"` JSONL of `session_quota_exceeded`. So R_IS_LIMIT fires, §15.2 step 2 calls `next`, and `next` records nothing but still returns another account with exit 0 (§9.3 table: `error` → nothing recorded; next never returns A with 0). Step 3 then switches to B. That is exactly the rotation R06 C11 forbids ("Do not rotate on session_quota_exceeded (a user cap)"), and it gets around the user's own `--max-ai-credits` cap.
fix: In §15.2 step 3, add: "0 with `recorded.class` `error` (for example Copilot `session_quota_exceeded`, §8.5): do not switch accounts. Keep A as the current account, delete the session file and run New with the handoff note, charged to maxRetriesOnError as an ordinary error." Alternatively, before step 2 for copilot, call `classify` and skip `next` when `rotate` is false. Add a §15.10 scenario: a copilot `session_quota_exceeded` run never changes the account.

where: §10.4 add flags: "| `--gh-host HOST` | `add copilot --kind gh` | string | `github.com` | the gh host, stored as `identity.host` (§8.5) |"
problem: §8.5 says "`--gh-host` (default `github.com`) is stored as `identity.host` for `token` and `gh` accounts", and §8.5 Environment and A.5 set `COPILOT_GH_HOST=<host>` for both the `token` and `gh` kinds. The §10.4 flag table allows `--gh-host` only with `add copilot --kind gh`. As written, a `token` (fine-grained PAT) account for a GitHub Enterprise host cannot be registered: the flag is a usage error (64) for it, so the FC#25 fix cannot be reached for the default copilot kind.
fix: Change the §10.4 row's Commands cell to `add copilot` (kinds `token` and `gh`), with the meaning "the GitHub host, stored as `identity.host`; a non-github.com host sets `COPILOT_GH_HOST` for runs (§8.5)". Keep `--gh-user` as `--kind gh` only.

where: §8.5 Environment, Secret isolation: "This is the only argument accshift ever adds (§7.6, §8), and the status file lists it in `addedArgs`."
problem: The FC#24 fix added a `run`-only exception: §16 step and §8.2 say `run` appends `--no-daemon` to codex TUI launches, and the §8 rules say "`run` has its own documented exception for codex `--no-daemon`". §8.5 still says the copilot secret-isolation flag is the only argument accshift *ever* adds, which contradicts §16, §8 and §8.2.
fix: Reword §8.5 to: "This is the only argument `exec` ever adds (§7.6, §8; `run` separately appends codex `--no-daemon`, §16), and the status file lists it in `addedArgs`."

where: §7.6: "`exec` reports it in the status file's `addedArgs`, and LimitShift's dry-run shows it."; §15.10 item 9: "dry-run prints the wrapped command, including `--status-file`"
problem: §7.6 says LimitShift's dry-run shows the added `--secret-env-vars` argument, but nothing in §15 does this. The dry-run (§15.3 single wrap point, §15.10 item 9) prints only the wrapped command `accshift exec copilot --account A --status-file … -- copilot …`, which never contains the argument, because exec adds it internally. A dry-run does not run exec, so no status file exists. §15 reads `addedArgs` only after a real run and logs it as INFO (§15.5). The §7.6 claim has no counterpart in §15.
fix: Either drop "and LimitShift's dry-run shows it" from §7.6 (keeping status-file `addedArgs` plus the INFO log of §15.5), or add to §15.3/§15.10 item 9: "for a copilot runner whose account kind (from `list --json`) is `token` or `gh`, dry-run also prints the note that exec will prepend `--secret-env-vars=COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`".

where: A.4 `native` row: "Unset `GEMINI_CLI_AUTH_OVERRIDE` when that `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` was unset, or when its value differs from the account's `nativeAuthOverride` (null = it was unset at `add --native`)"; the same wording appears in §8.4 ("is unset when that `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` was unset") and §12.5

where: Appendix D.4 (90-appendices.md lines 210-237) vs §11.2 (10-cli-contract.md lines 234-340). Examples: D.4 "AccountEntry ... {name, kind, label?, state, ...}"; D.4 "`list <cli>`: {contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, accounts:[AccountEntry]}"; D.4 "`status [cli]`: the list shape, plus top-level vault:{...} and agySlot?:{...}"; D.4 "accounts:[{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}]"; D.4 "`next`: ... switched = (account ≠ previous)"; §11.2 "`postRunError`: null, or {code, message}"; D.4 "Status file (`exec` / `run --status-file PATH`...)"
problem:
CP#26 added the full shapes to §11.2, but Appendix D.4, which §18.2 uses as the schema for every §11 response, now disagrees with §11.2 in several places, so the schema test cannot pass both:
(1) §11.2 list entries carry `id` ("An account entry has: name, id ..."); D.4 AccountEntry has no `id`.
(2) The §11.2 list example has `poolDropped:[]`; D.4 `list` has no `poolDropped`.
(3) §11.2 status adds top-level `notice:{accepted, version, acceptedAt, acceptedAtEpoch}`, plus per-account `relogin`, `attentionCode`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt`, `lastOkAt` and `utilization`. D.4 status has none of these. §15.7 item 6 reads `notice.accepted` from `status --json`.
(4) §11.2 puts `agySlot` "in the agy per-cli object" (the no-cli form is `{contract, vault, notice, clis}`); D.4 makes it top-level.
(5) pick/next `accounts[]` entries: §11.2 `{name, state, reason, limitedUntil, limitedUntilEpoch, limits}`; D.4 `{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}`.
(6) `recorded`: §11.2 includes `relogin` and `attentionCode`; D.4 omits both.
(7) `switched` for next: on 69/77 `account` is null. D.4's `account ≠ previous` yields true; §11.2 says true only when both are non-null and differ.
(8) Status file `postRunError`: §11.2 says `{code, message}`, while §12.1.1 and D.4 say `{code, reason}`.
(9) D.4 says `exec` / `run --status-file`, but §10.4 lists `--status-file` for `exec` only, and the §16 `run` syntax has no such flag.
fix:
Make Appendix D.4 match §11.2 exactly:
- AccountEntry gains `id`.
- `list <cli>` gains `poolDropped:[name]`.
- `status [cli]` = the list shape plus top-level `vault:{exists, keySource?, keyId?, keyFilePath?}` and `notice:{accepted, version?, acceptedAt?, acceptedAtEpoch?}`. The agy per-cli object carries `agySlot?:{owner?, store?, writtenAt?, writtenAtEpoch?, saveBackPending}`. Every status AccountEntry adds `relogin?:{reason, since, sinceEpoch}`, `attentionCode?`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt?`/`lastStrikeAtEpoch?`, `lastOkAt?`/`lastOkAtEpoch?` and `utilization?`; agy entries also add `wrongAccount?`.
- pick/next/mark `accounts:[{name, state, reason?, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?, limits:[Limit]}]`.
- `recorded` adds `relogin?` and `attentionCode?`.
- `next`: "switched is true when account and previous are both non-null and differ".
- Status file: write `(exec --status-file PATH, §12.1.1)`, dropping `run`.
In §11.2, change the status-file bullet to "`postRunError`: null, or `{code, reason}` when a post-run hook failed".

where: §10.4 row "`--gh-host HOST` | `add copilot --kind gh` | string | `github.com` | the gh host, stored as `identity.host`" vs §8.5 Add "`--gh-host` (default `github.com`) is stored as `identity.host` for `token` and `gh` accounts" and Appendix A.5 `token`, `gh`: "When `identity.host` is not `github.com`, set `COPILOT_GH_HOST=<host>`". §8.2 "**Add** (`accshift add codex <name> [--browser] [--import-home DIR] [--label L] [--accept-notice]`): 1. A TTY is required." §8.5 "A failure exits 65 with the helper's code (`classic-pat-unsupported` or `gh-token-unavailable`)". D-07 "Copilot uses `--from-gh`"
problem:
The flag table and the adapter text still disagree, and some flows are still undefined.
(1) §10.4 restricts `--gh-host` to `--kind gh`. §8.5 and A.5, however, store and use `identity.host` for `token` accounts too, so a GitHub Enterprise `token` account cannot set its host.
(2) The §8.2 codex add syntax omits `--native`, `--kind access-token|api-key` and `--token-stdin`, all of which §10.4 assigns to `add codex`. §8.2 also defines no add flow for the `access-token` and `api-key` kinds: no secret read, no vault write and no `at-` check. Yet §8.2 Login says "read the new secret as at add (no-echo TTY or `--token-stdin`)", and add step 1 says "A TTY is required", which contradicts `--token-stdin`.
(3) `gh-token-unavailable` is used as a 65 code for `add copilot --kind gh`, but the §10.3 row 65 and the Appendix E row 65 do not list it.
(4) D-07 still names the undefined flag `--from-gh`.
fix:
(1) §10.4 `--gh-host` row: Commands = `add copilot` (`token` and `gh` kinds), meaning "the GitHub host, stored as `identity.host` (§8.5)".
(2) §8.2 Add syntax: `accshift add codex <name> [--native | --kind home|access-token|api-key] [--browser] [--import-home DIR] [--label L] [--token-stdin] [--accept-notice]`. Add a step: "`access-token`, `api-key`: read the secret from a no-echo TTY prompt or one line of `--token-stdin` (no TTY needed), validate the `at-` prefix and record the expiry for `access-token`, and store it as `codex/<id>`; `--label` is required." Restrict step 1's TTY requirement to the `home` kind.
(3) Add `gh-token-unavailable` (`add copilot --kind gh`) to the §10.3 row 65 and the Appendix E row 65.
(4) In D-07, replace `--from-gh` with "the copilot `gh` kind".

where: §21 M1 exit criteria: "every §11 response validates against Appendix D; the §18.4 NFR1 and size gates pass on every runner" vs §18.4: "every NFR1 command without the vault (`version`, `list`, `pick`, `next`, `mark`, `status`, `classify`, each with `--json`): gated at 50 ms; `exec` of a fake CLI for a claude `token` account ...; one vault-touching command (`exec` of a `token` account) per key source ...: gated at 150 ms"
problem: The new testable M1 criteria require gates for commands that M1 does not deliver. M1's scope lists `version/list/status/doctor/pick/next/mark/enable/disable/order/config` and vault work. `exec`, the claude `token` kind, `classify claude`, the status file and `env` arrive only in M2. So "the §18.4 NFR1 ... gates pass" (which include `classify` and `exec` of a `token` account) and "every §11 response validates" (including `classify`, `env`, the exec status file) cannot be met when M1 closes. The criteria are unachievable as written.
fix: M1 exit criteria: "every §11 response of the commands M1 delivers validates against Appendix D; the §18.4 size gate and the 50 ms gate for `version`, `list`, `pick`, `next`, `mark` and `status` pass on every runner". Add to M2's exit criteria: "the remaining §18.4 NFR1 gates (`classify`, `exec` overhead, the 150 ms vault-touching `exec` per key source) pass, and the `classify`, `env` and status-file responses validate against Appendix D".

where: §9.2 Success: "`exec` never reports success ... Its only state writes are `relogin(missing)` for an absent credential, and the agy post-run bookkeeping: `agySlot`, `wrongAccount`, `relogin(rejected)` on an emptied slot, and `saveBackPending` (§8.3.3, §12.1)."
problem: CP#21's fix makes `exec` cache the agy version in `state.agyBinary` under `state.lock` on a cache miss (§8.3.1, §6.3). §6.3 ("exec writes only relogin(missing) ..., the agy post-run bookkeeping ... and the `agyBinary` cache") and §12.1 ("Its only state.json writes are ... and the `agyBinary` cache (§8.3.1)") list that write. §9.2's exhaustive "only state writes" list omits it, so the three normative lists disagree.
fix: In §9.2, change the sentence to: "Its only state writes are `relogin(missing)` for an absent credential, the agy bookkeeping (`agySlot`, `wrongAccount`, `relogin(rejected)` on an emptied slot, `saveBackPending`) and the `agyBinary` cache (§8.3.1, §8.3.3, §12.1)."

where: §11.1 rule 8: read-only commands "take no lock and make no state, vendor or file-system write ... and never create the root"; §10.1: "`--debug`: redacted debug log to stderr and `logs/`"; §6.1 tree: "logs/accshift.log only with --debug or ACCSHIFT_DEBUG=1"
problem: `--debug` is a global flag, and `ACCSHIFT_DEBUG=1` an environment switch, that writes `<root>/logs/accshift.log` for any command. The spec states no exception for read-only commands. So `accshift pick claude --debug` would write, and possibly create, `logs/` and the root, which contradicts rule 8 and the §18.2 test "read-only commands ... never take a lock or write ... anything".
fix: In §10.1 (`--debug`) and §11.1 rule 8, add: "Read-only commands write the debug log to stderr only; only writers append to `logs/accshift.log`." Alternatively, state the debug log as an explicit exception to rule 8 that never creates the root, and adjust the §18.2 read-only test to match.

where: Appendix D.4: AccountEntry "`{name, kind, label?, state:…, reason?, enabled, usageProbe, …}`"; "**`list <cli>`:** `{contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, accounts:[AccountEntry]}`"; "**`status [cli]`:** the `list` shape, plus top-level `vault:{…}` … and `agySlot?:{owner?, store?, writtenAt?, writtenAtEpoch?, saveBackPending}`"; "`next`: `previous` = `--from`; `switched` = (`account` ≠ `previous`)"; "`recorded`: null for `pick` and for an unknown `--from` / `--account`; otherwise `{account, class, kind?, scope?, until?, untilEpoch?, tier?, limitSource?, resetConfidence?, limitType?}`. When nothing was stored …, `class` names the evidence class"
problem: §18.2 validates every §11 response against D.4, but D.4 disagrees with §11.2 in several places. (1) §11.2 says "An account entry has: `name`, `id` (immutable, §6.2), …", and the list example carries `"id"`, but AccountEntry has no `id`. (2) The §11.2 list object has `"poolDropped":[]`, but D.4 `list` lacks it. (3) §11.2 status adds top-level `notice: {accepted, version, acceptedAt, acceptedAtEpoch}`, which §15.7 item 6 reads (`notice.accepted:false`), but D.4 has no `notice`. (4) §11.2 puts `agySlot` "in the agy per-cli object", while D.4 puts it at the top level. (5) §11.2 adds to every status account entry `relogin`, `attentionCode`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt`/`lastStrikeAtEpoch`, `lastOkAt`/`lastOkAtEpoch` and `utilization`, none of which D.4 has. (6) §11.2 `recorded` has `relogin` and `attentionCode`, but D.4 lacks them. §11.2 also gives `recorded.class` as `ok`/`clear` for mark, which are not evidence classes. (7) D.4's `switched` = (account ≠ previous) makes a 69/77 `next` (account null) switched:true. §11.2 says "true when `account` and `previous` are both non-null and differ". (8) D.4 says `recorded` is null for an unknown `--account`, but §10.3 makes an unknown `mark --account` or `classify --record --account` exit 64 with the plain error object, so that case never reaches the response shape.
fix: In D.4: AccountEntry gains `id`. `list <cli>` becomes `{contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, poolDropped:[name], accounts:[AccountEntry]}`. `status [cli]` becomes: "the `list` shape plus top-level `vault:{exists, keySource?, keyId?, keyFilePath?}` and `notice:{accepted, version?, acceptedAt?, acceptedAtEpoch?}`; the agy per-cli object adds `agySlot?:{owner?, store?, writtenAt?, writtenAtEpoch?, saveBackPending}`; every status AccountEntry adds `relogin?:{reason, since, sinceEpoch}`, `attentionCode?`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt?`, `lastStrikeAtEpoch?`, `lastOkAt?`, `lastOkAtEpoch?`, `utilization?`, and for agy `wrongAccount?`". `recorded` gains `relogin?` and `attentionCode?`, with the sentence "`class` is the evidence class, or `limit`/`auth` from the flags, or `ok`/`clear` for `mark --ok`/`--clear`". Replace the `switched` bullet with "`switched` is true when `account` and `previous` are both non-null and differ". Change "unknown `--from` / `--account`" to "unknown `--from`".

where: Appendix D.4 pick/next/mark: "`accounts:[{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}]`" vs §11.2: "Each entry is `{name, state, reason, limitedUntil, limitedUntilEpoch, limits}` with the `list` meanings" and §9.1: "`list`, `status` and `accounts[]` report every active record as `limits:[…]`"

where: §8.3.2: "the swap is refused before any write, with `exec` exit 125 `slot-write-failed` (control verbs 74)"; §8.3.3 B.5: "any other write error, such as a full disk → 125 `slot-write-failed` (74)"; §13.3: "fails with 125 `slot-write-failed` (control verbs 74)"; §8.3.3 B.8: "exit 125 `slot-write-failed` (macOS prompt: `keychain-prompt-required`)" (no control-verb code, though `agy use`, `add agy` and `login agy` run B.8); §8.5: "A failure exits 65 with the helper's code (`classic-pat-unsupported` or `gh-token-unavailable`)"; §7.4: "for accshift's own key, fail with `error.code = \"keychain-line-too-long\"`" vs §10.3 74: "`keystore-unavailable` (…), `vault-changed`, `agy-keyring-locked`, or a missing passphrase"; §10.3/Appendix E 65 lists without `gh-token-unavailable`; Appendix E 74: "a failed agy slot or vault write"
problem: Sections use control-verb error codes that neither §10.3 nor Appendix E lists. `slot-write-failed` is a 74 in three places. `keychain-prompt-required` has no control-verb exit at all. `gh-token-unavailable` is a 65 for `add`/`login copilot --kind gh`. `keychain-line-too-long` has an error.code but no exit code anywhere. D.4 ties every `error.code` to Appendix E, so the schema cannot accept these codes.
fix: §10.3 row 74 and Appendix E row 74: add "`slot-write-failed` (an agy slot write or its verification failed and was rolled back, or a vault write failed for another reason; §8.3.2, §8.3.3 B.5/B.8, §13.3), `keychain-prompt-required` (§8.3.3 B.8), `keychain-line-too-long` (§7.4)", and in Appendix E replace "a failed agy slot or vault write" with those names. §8.3.3 B.8: "… exit 125 `slot-write-failed` (macOS prompt: `keychain-prompt-required`); control verbs exit 74 with the same code". §7.4: "fail with exit 74 `keychain-line-too-long`". §10.3 row 65 and Appendix E row 65: add "`gh-token-unavailable` (`add`/`login copilot --kind gh`, §8.5)".

where: §8.1: "`add --native` refuses it with exit 78 and the hint to unset `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`"; §8.2 add step 7: "If the shared config sets `cli_auth_credentials_store = \"ephemeral\"`, refuse overlays (exit 78)"; §8.2 Homes: "Initialising `mainHome` … MUST refuse (exit 78) a directory whose canonical path is inside `<root>/homes/`"; §8.2 Import: "If the unlink fails, delete the copy and abort with exit 73" and "It refuses if DIR is `mainHome` or any codex process or daemon is using DIR" (no code) vs §11.1 rule 5 (every failure prints `error.code`) and §10.3 78: "`config-corrupt`, `config-newer-version`, `insecure-permissions`, `wrong-owner`, `unsupported-filesystem`, `vault-corrupt`, `vault-corrupt-present`, `key-item-exists`"
problem: These control-verb refusals have an exit code but no `error.code`, or no exit code at all, and none of the §10.3 / Appendix E codes describes them. A JSON error object cannot be produced for them. An unlink failure is not a "busy" condition, yet it is put under 73.
fix: Name and list them. §10.3 row 78 and Appendix E row 78: add "`unsupported-config` (`add claude --native` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set but empty; a codex `ephemeral` credential store; a codex `mainHome` inside `<root>/homes/` at its first initialisation)", and use that code in §8.1 and §8.2. §8.2 Import: "refuses with 73 `overlay-in-use` when a codex process or daemon uses DIR, and with 65 `invalid-import` when DIR is `mainHome`". For the EXDEV unlink failure: "abort with exit 74 `import-failed`", with each new code added to §10.3 and Appendix E.

where: §7.3 Key-file checks: "otherwise exit 78 with the fix (`exec`: 125 `keystore-unavailable`)" vs §12.1.1 `keystore-unavailable`: "… a missing key item or key file, a failed key-file check …"; §10.3 74: "`keystore-unavailable` (… key file missing; timeout)"; §7.3 Rules: "exit 74 for control verbs, exit 125 with `keystore-unavailable` for `exec`"; §7.5: "Failures end in exit 74 (control verbs) or 125 `keystore-unavailable` (`exec`)"
problem: A key file with the wrong owner or mode gives control verbs 78 with no `error.code`, while exec reports the same condition as `keystore-unavailable`, which §10.3 puts under 74. One condition therefore has two different control-verb codes, depending on whether you read §7.3 or §12.1.1/§10.3. None of §10.3's 78 codes fits.
fix: §7.3: "otherwise exit 74 `keystore-unavailable` with the fix (`exec`: 125 `keystore-unavailable`)". In §10.3 row 74, change "key file missing" to "key file missing, or with a wrong owner or mode".

where: §8.2 Homes: "Initialising `mainHome` and `config clis.codex.mainHome` MUST refuse (exit 78) a directory whose canonical path is inside `<root>/homes/`" vs §10.2 config: "An invalid value exits 65 and changes nothing"; §6.2: "An invalid value exits 65 and changes nothing"; §10.3 65: "an invalid `config` value or edit"; Appendix E 65: "an invalid config value"
problem: The same command and condition, an invalid value for `config clis.codex.mainHome`, is exit 78 in §8.2 and exit 65 in §10.2, §6.2, §10.3 and Appendix E.
fix: §8.2: "`config clis.codex.mainHome` refuses such a directory with 65 (an invalid config value, §10.2). Initialising `mainHome` from an inherited `CODEX_HOME` at the first codex `add` refuses it with 78 `unsupported-config` (§10.3)."

where: §12.2: "`ACCSHIFT_<CLI>_BIN` and `clis.<cli>.bin` MUST be absolute paths; a relative value is a usage error (64; 125 `usage` for `exec` and `run`)"; §12.1.1 `usage`: "a relative `--home`, `ACCSHIFT_HOME`, `ACCSHIFT_<CLI>_BIN` or `clis.<cli>.bin`" vs D.1: "`bin`: absolute path of the vendor binary (§12.2)"; §6.2: "accshift validates it on every load against Appendix D.1"; §6.4: "A file that parses but fails validation (Appendix D.1, D.2) is never renamed. Commands exit 78 `config-corrupt` naming the field (`exec`: 125)"
problem: A relative `clis.<cli>.bin` in accounts.json is a registry value that fails D.1 validation (78 `config-corrupt` per §6.4; `config` rejects it with 65). §12.2 and §12.1.1 call the same state a usage error (64 / 125 `usage`). Callers would see different codes for one condition.
fix: §12.2: "`ACCSHIFT_<CLI>_BIN` MUST be absolute; a relative value is a usage error (64; 125 `usage` for `exec` and `run`). `clis.<cli>.bin` MUST be absolute: `config` rejects a relative value (65), and a relative value in accounts.json fails validation (78 `config-corrupt`; exec 125 `config-corrupt`, §6.4)." Remove `clis.<cli>.bin` from the §12.1.1 `usage` row.

where: §15.7: "`--validate-only` calls only read-only commands (`version`, `list`, `status`, `pick`, `doctor --json`; §11.1 rule 8)." and item 8 "agy model discovery follows §15.5 and never swaps the slot." vs §15.5: "`agy models` and `--probe-models` run through `accshift exec agy --account X` … exec takes the shared fast path for it, which writes no slot (§8.3.3)"; §11.1 rule 8 lists `exec` among writers; §13.1: shared mode "only … when V-A8 has passed"
problem: Validate-only runs `exec agy`, which is a writer. It writes the vault save-back and the `agyBinary` cache, takes the slot lock, and on the exclusive path runs the foreign-process check. This contradicts the read-only rule. The shared fast path exists only after V-A8 has passed. Before that, exec takes the exclusive path, so with the user's own agy open it fails 125 `agy-busy`, and no validate-only outcome is specified for that failure.
fix: §15.7 first sentence: "`--validate-only` calls only read-only commands …, plus, for agy model discovery, one `exec agy --account <the account `pick agy` returned>` (§15.5). It never swaps, but it may write the vault save-back and state.json. Any 125 from it (for example `agy-busy`) is a WARNING, and the cached capabilities are used." §15.5: "exec takes the shared fast path once V-A8 has passed, else the exclusive path; since the slot already holds that account, neither path writes a slot."

where: §11.2: "LimitShift's auto mode routes an experimental cli only when the runner lists `accounts` explicitly"; §9.3: "LimitShift's auto mode routes a runner through accshift only when `rotationPossible` is true, or the runner names accounts explicitly (§15.4)"; D-03 Risks: "auto mode routing a runner without explicit `accounts` only when `rotationPossible` is true"; §15.4: "**`experimental` clis** … are routed under `auto` only when the runner lists `accounts` explicitly"; §15.7 item 4: "An `experimental` CLI → WARNING when the runner lists `accounts` …, else INFO \"not routed (experimental)\"; ERROR under `required` without `accounts`" vs §15.4 agy rule: "an agy runner without `accounts` counts as listing every agy account, so it is routed even when agy is `experimental` or `rotationPossible` is false" and §15.3 acct_decide "or when the cli is agy with agy accounts registered"
problem: agy is `experimental` on every OS until its V-A items pass (§8.3.5). While agy accounts are registered, an agy runner without `accounts` is routed under both auto and required, whatever `rotationPossible` says. Five statements give the unqualified rule instead: explicit `accounts` only, or `rotationPossible`. Read literally, validate-only prints INFO "not routed" (auto) or ERROR (required) for a runner that will in fact be routed.
fix: In §11.2, §9.3, D-03 and the §15.4 experimental bullet, append "(except agy while agy accounts are registered, §15.4)". §15.7 item 4: add "an agy runner while agy accounts are registered and its `accounts` key absent → WARNING 'routed; rotation unverified on this OS', never INFO 'not routed' or ERROR".

where: §15.2 exec table: "| every other code; also 126 and 127 | needs-human, no retry |" vs §15.3 bash: "if [ \"$R_EXIT\" = 125 ] && [ \"$ACCT_LAUNCHED\" != true ]; then acct_outcome exec 125 \"$ACCT_ERR\"" and ps1: "the post-run hooks (125 check, then `wrongAccount` and `mark --ok`)"
problem: The normative hooks check only for 125. An accshift 126 (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`) or 127 (`not-found`) with `launched:false` goes down the normal CLI result path (classify, then the retry budget) instead of needs-human, so the hooks contradict the §15.2 table.
fix: §15.3 bash: `case $R_EXIT in 125|126|127) if [ "$ACCT_LAUNCHED" != true ]; then acct_outcome exec "$R_EXIT" "$ACCT_ERR"; case $? in 1) …;; 2) <needs-human> ;; 3) <busy-limited> ;; esac; fi ;; esac`. ps1 bullet: "(125–127 check when `launched` is false, then `wrongAccount` and `mark --ok`)". v2: the status-file read applies the same 125–127 table.

where: §11.3 bash recipe: `next claude --from "$acct" --model "$next_model" --limited-model "$model" --evidence-file … --run-started-at "$run_start" ${pool:+…} ${parsed_reset:+…} --json` and the PowerShell `$acctArgs = @('next', 'claude', …)` (no `--session`/`--cwd`); §11.2: "(`next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0` at 10:40Z…)" with `"tier":3,"limitSource":"structured"` vs §15.2 step 2: "`--session` … and `--cwd` … are passed for claude and codex"; §15.3: `case $run_cli in claude|codex) … args+=(--session "$sid" --cwd "$project_path")`; §10.4 `--cwd` default "none (no Claude transcript lookup)"; D-08 r5: "Claude's `rate_limit_event` appears only in stream-json, while LimitShift uses `--output-format json`"
problem: §11.3 presents itself as LimitShift's recipe ("LimitShift exports …"), yet its claude `next` call omits `--session`/`--cwd`, which §15.2 and §15.3 require for claude and codex. The §11.2 example call has no transcript lookup either, so with LimitShift's json-mode evidence it cannot produce the tier-3 `structured` record it shows. §5.2 runs the same scenario with `--session U --cwd D` for exactly this reason.
fix: §11.2: change the call to `next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0 --session U --cwd D`. §11.3 bash: add `${sid:+--session "$sid" --cwd "$project_path"}`. ps1: add `if ($sid) { $acctArgs += @('--session', $sid, '--cwd', $projectPath) }`. Note both as "claude and codex only (§15.2)".

where: §6.3: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok`, a same-identity `login` and `mark --clear` clear them." and "A same-identity `login` clears `relogin`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt` and auth-suspect records" vs §9.2 Success: mark --ok "keeps limit records, `relogin`, `attentionCode` and `lastStrikeAt` (the incident window of other accounts still sees that strike)"; §9.2 Login effects and §8 Login rules: "A same-identity `login` clears `relogin`, `authStrikes` and auth-suspect records"
problem: §6.3 has `mark --ok` and same-identity `login` clear `lastStrikeAt`, while §9.2 and §8 keep it. The incident rule (§9.2 step 2) counts accounts by `lastStrikeAt`. Under §6.3, a success on one account hides its strike, so a provider outage could escalate the other accounts instead of being treated as an incident.
fix: §6.3: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok` and a same-identity `login` clear `authStrikes` and keep `lastStrikeAt` (incident window, §9.2); `mark --clear` and `login --new-identity` clear both." Remove `lastStrikeAt` from the §6.3 same-identity-login sentence.

where: §6.3 example `claude/3f9a01c2`: `"model:opus": { "hits": 0, "lastUntil": 1791784800, "lastHitAt": 1791368400, … }` (10:20Z) with `"lastOkAt": 1791369000` (10:30Z) vs §6.3 "`lastOkAt` is written only by `mark --ok`" and "`mark --ok` and `mark --clear` delete the whole map"; §9.2/§10.2 mark --ok "clears … the `backoff` map"
problem: The 10:30Z `mark --ok` would have deleted the 10:20Z `model:opus` backoff entry, so the 10:45Z snapshot cannot contain it. §18.1's example-pair test and golden files would copy an impossible state.
fix: Set `lastOkAt` to a time before the Opus hit, for example `1791367800` (2026-10-07T10:10:00Z).

where: §9.4: "Pruning removes expired records but keeps a backoff entry until 24 h after its `lastHitAt`" and "**Early re-hit** …: a limit hit while `lastUntil ≤ now < lastUntil + 15 min`"; §6.3: "Pruning keeps an entry until 24 h after its `lastHitAt`"; §6.3 example `model:opus` lastHitAt 1791368400, lastUntil 1791784800
problem: For any record longer than about 24 h (Claude `seven_day_opus`/`seven_day_sonnet`, Copilot weekly or monthly quotas), the entry holding `lastUntil` is pruned before the record expires. The early re-hit rule can then never fire for that scope. The §6.3 example shows it: the opus entry is pruned at 1791454800 (Oct 8 10:20Z), almost four days before its `lastUntil` (Oct 12 06:00Z).
fix: In §9.4 and §6.3: "A backoff entry is kept until max(`lastHitAt` + 24 h, `lastUntil` + 15 min)." §9.4 counters: "`hits` and `rehitMinutes` reset on `mark --ok`, or when their entry is pruned; `authStrikes` after 24 h without a new strike". Add an §18.1 case: a 7-day record expires, and a hit within 15 minutes applies the early re-hit backoff.

where: §7.1: "**Account metadata lives outside the vault**, in `accounts.json` / `state.json`: ids, names, kinds, labels, limits, expiry dates and optional 8-hex fingerprints." vs D.1 Account and D.2 AccountState (no fingerprint field); D.3: vault entry `{type, value, createdAt, updatedAt, fingerprint}`; §8.5: "A token whose vault `fingerprint` (Appendix D.3) equals another copilot account's"
problem: §7.1 places fingerprints in accounts.json/state.json, but neither schema has such a field, and D.3 and §8.5 keep the fingerprint in the vault entry. The tier2-appendices editor asked for this change; it was not made.
fix: §7.1: "… ids, names, kinds, labels, limits and expiry dates. Secret fingerprints live in the vault entries (Appendix D.3)."

where: D-03 requirements: "Capabilities (`sessionPortable`, `usageProbe`, `lockScope`, `dataDir`) appear in `version`/`list`." vs §11.2 / D.4: `capabilities:{<cli>:{sessionPortable, lockScope, usageProbe, dataDir?}}` only in `version`; list entries carry a per-account boolean `usageProbe` and no `sessionPortable`, `lockScope` or `dataDir`

fix: D-03: "Capabilities (`sessionPortable`, `usageProbe`, `lockScope`, `dataDir`) appear in `version --json` `capabilities`; `list` entries carry a per-account `usageProbe` flag."

where: §6.2 accounts.json example: codex `{ "name": "main", "id": "52a8c1f0", "kind": "native", …, "enabled": true }`, codex `work` (`c81f4a6d`) and agy `a` (`7c41d09e`) entries have no `createdAt` vs D.1: "`Account = {id, name, kind, label?, plan?, enabled, createdAt, expiresAt?, …}`" (createdAt required) and §6.2 "accshift validates it on every load against Appendix D.1"
problem: Three of the five example accounts omit the required `createdAt`. The example registry would fail its own validation (78 `config-corrupt`), and the §18.1 example test would pick it up.
fix: Add `"createdAt"` to the codex `main`, codex `work` and agy `a` entries, for example `"2026-10-06T08:00:00Z"`, `"2026-10-06T08:10:00Z"` and `"2026-10-06T08:20:00Z"`, which are before their state.json activity.

where: §5.2: "limitshift ──exec claude --account work … (run starts 09:00Z = 1791363600)" and "--run-started-at 1791363600", with "The accounts are those of the §11.2 scenario" vs §6.2 accounts.json `work` (`3f9a01c2`): `"createdAt": "2026-10-07T10:05:00Z"`
problem: In the shared scenario, the run on `work` starts at 09:00Z on 2026-10-07, but `work` was registered at 10:05Z that day. `expiresAt` 2027-10-07T10:05:00Z and §11.2's `expiresAtEpoch` 1822903500 depend on that createdAt. The example timeline is impossible.
fix: §5.2: "(run starts 10:25Z = 1791368700)" and "--run-started-at 1791368700". This is after the 10:20Z Opus record and before the 10:40Z limit.

where: §11.2 exec --status-file field list: "`postRunError`: `null`, or `{code, message}` when a post-run hook failed."
problem: §12.1.1 ("`postRunError`: null, or `{code, reason}` for a failed or skipped post-run hook") and Appendix D.4 ("postRunError?:{code, reason?}") use `{code, reason}`. §18.2 checks every response against D.4, so a status file built from §11.2 fails that check. LimitShift (§15.5) logs this field.
fix: In §11.2 replace the bullet with: "`postRunError`: `null`, or `{code, reason}` for a failed or skipped post-run hook (for example `save-back-failed`, `copy-back-skipped`). Post-run failures never change the exit status."

where: Appendix D.4 pick/next/mark: "`next`: `previous` = `--from`; `switched` = (`account` ≠ `previous`)."
problem: On next's 69 and 77, `account` is null and `previous` is A, so D.4 gives `switched:true`. §11.2 says "`switched`: true when `account` and `previous` are both non-null and differ", so §11.2 gives false. LimitShift's own code reads `account`, but a schema or golden test built from D.4 disagrees with §11.2.
fix: In D.4 write: "`next`: `previous` = `--from`; `switched` is true only when `account` and `previous` are both non-null and differ (so false on 69, 77, and on 75 naming `--from`)."

where: Appendix D.4: AccountEntry "{name, kind, label?, state…}" (no id); "`list <cli>`: {contract, cli, poolSize, rotationPossible, accounts:[AccountEntry]}"; "`status [cli]`: … plus top-level vault:{…} and agySlot?:{…}"; pick/next "accounts:[{name, state, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?}]"; recorded "{account, class, kind?, … limitType?}"
problem: D.4 disagrees with §11.2 on fields that the flows read. (1) §11.2 puts `notice:{accepted, version, acceptedAt, acceptedAtEpoch}` at the top level of `status`, and §15.7 item 6 reads `notice.accepted`. D.4 has no `notice`. (2) §11.2 puts `agySlot` in the agy per-cli object; D.4 puts it at the top level. (3) §11.2 status account entries carry relogin, attentionCode, authStrikes, lastStrikeAt, lastOkAt and utilization; D.4 has none of them. (4) §11.2 list entries have `id`, and the list object has `poolDropped`. (5) §11.2 pick/next accounts[] are `{name, state, reason, limitedUntil, limitedUntilEpoch, limits}`. (6) §11.2 `recorded` carries `relogin` and `attentionCode`. §18.2 asserts every §11 response against Appendix D.
fix: Make D.4 match §11.2 exactly. Add `id` to AccountEntry. Add `poolDropped:[name]` to the list per-cli object. In `status`: add top-level `notice:{accepted, version?, acceptedAt?, acceptedAtEpoch?}`; move `agySlot?:{owner?, store?, writtenAt?, writtenAtEpoch?, saveBackPending}` into the agy per-cli object; add `relogin?:{reason, since, sinceEpoch}, attentionCode?, authStrikes, lastStrikeAt?, lastStrikeAtEpoch?, lastOkAt?, lastOkAtEpoch?, utilization?` to each status account entry. Make pick/next/mark accounts[] `{name, state, reason?, limitedUntil?, limitedUntilEpoch?, limits:[Limit]}`. Add `relogin?` and `attentionCode?` to `recorded`.

where: Appendix D.4: "**Status file** (`exec` / `run --status-file PATH`, §12.1.1; …)"
problem: §10.4 lists `--status-file P` for `exec` only. The `run` syntax in §10.2 and §16 (`run <cli> [--account A] [--pool a,b] [--slot-wait S] [--wait] -- <args…>`) has no such flag, and §10.1 makes unknown flags a 125 `usage` error for run.
fix: In D.4 write "**Status file** (`exec --status-file PATH`, §12.1.1; …)". Alternatively, add `--status-file` to `run` in §10.2, §10.4 and §16, but not one without the others.

where: §7.5: "- `exec` and `run` never prompt, whatever stdin is. Any condition that would need input takes the non-interactive branch…"
problem: §16 step 6 says "`run` MAY ask whether to switch and resume, only when stdin is a TTY and `ACCSHIFT_NONINTERACTIVE` is not `1`". §10.1 and Appendix A.0 say the same, and so does the amendment. §7.5 forbids any prompt from `run`.
fix: In §7.5 write: "`exec` never prompts, whatever stdin is. `run` never prompts during pre-launch credential handling; it MAY ask its §16 step-6 question only when stdin is a TTY and `ACCSHIFT_NONINTERACTIVE` is not `1`. Any other condition that would need input takes the non-interactive branch…"

where: §15.3 bash hook: "if [ \"$R_EXIT\" = 125 ] && [ \"$ACCT_LAUNCHED\" != true ]; then acct_outcome exec 125 …"; ps1 "the post-run hooks (125 check, then wrongAccount and mark --ok)"; v2 "reads the status file (125 table, §15.2)"
problem: The §15.2 table says "every other code; also 126 and 127 | needs-human, no retry", and Appendix E rows 126/127 also say needs-human. The hooks test only `R_EXIT = 125`. An exec 126 (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`) or 127 (`not-found`) with `launched:false` therefore falls through to the error branch. It runs `classify` on a run that never started and spends maxRetriesOnError, instead of marking the task needs-human.
fix: In §15.3 (sh, ps1 and v2) change the check to "when `R_EXIT` is 125, 126 or 127 and `ACCT_LAUNCHED` is not `true`", and call `acct_outcome exec "$R_EXIT" "$ACCT_ERR"`, which maps 126 and 127 to return 2 (needs-human). Retitle the §15.2 block "exec exit 125–127 with `launched:false`". Add a §15.10 scenario: exec 127 `not-found` marks the task needs-human without calling `classify`.

where: §10.3: "126: the cli was found but is not executable (`not-executable`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found"; Appendix E: "| 127 | cli not found | exec, run | needs-human |"
problem: §12.1.1 defines 126 as `not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported` or `wsl-windows-binary`, and 127 as `not-found`. §10.3 omits `cmd-shim-unsupported` and has no code for 127. Appendix E's 127 row also has no code. LimitShift reads `error.code` from the status file for these exits.
fix: In §10.3 write "126: … (`not-executable`, `cmd-shim-unsupported`, `wsl-windows-binary`). 127: the cli was not found (`not-found`)". In Appendix E write "| 127 | cli not found: `not-found` (§12.2) | exec, run | needs-human |".

where: §6.3 AccountState: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok`, a same-identity `login` and `mark --clear` clear them."; also "A same-identity `login` clears `relogin`, `authStrikes`, `lastStrikeAt` and auth-suspect records"
problem: §9.2 says `mark --ok` "keeps limit records, `relogin`, `attentionCode` and `lastStrikeAt` (the incident window of other accounts still sees that strike)". §9.2, §8 and D4 list a same-identity login as clearing only `relogin`, `authStrikes` and auth-suspect records. Under §6.3's wording, an account struck just before it succeeded drops out of the §9.2 step-2 incident count, so a second account's strike within `authSuspectMinutes` escalates instead of being treated as an incident.
fix: In §6.3 write: "`authStrikes` and `lastStrikeAt`: … `mark --ok` and a same-identity `login` clear `authStrikes` and keep `lastStrikeAt` (the incident window, §9.2); `mark --clear` clears both." Remove `lastStrikeAt` from the login sentence.

where: §11.2: "(`next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0` at 10:40Z…)", whose `recorded` is "tier":3,"limitSource":"structured"
problem: For claude, tier-3 data comes only from a stream-json `rate_limit_event` or the transcript's `rate_limit_info` (§8.1, Appendix C.1). LimitShift uses `--output-format json` (D8 reason 5), and the transcript is read only with `--session`/`--cwd` (§9.5; §10.4 `--cwd` default: "no Claude transcript lookup"). The example call passes neither, so it can record only tier 2 `text`. §5.2 passes `--session U --cwd D` for this same scenario.
fix: Change the example call to `next claude --from work --model M --evidence-file F --exit 1 --run-started-at T0 --session U --cwd D`. The recorded tier-3 `structured` record then matches §5.2 and §9.4.

where: §8.3.4 login agy Identity: "Otherwise the new credential is parked as `agy/_unregistered/<email>`, and after step 6 the command exits 65 `identity-mismatch`."
problem: §7.2 defines `agy/_unregistered/<email>` as "slot content for an email that no agy account has". B.5 stores a registered email under that account's `agy/<id>`, and §13.3 recovery of the same `op:"add"` journal saves "a registered email to that account, else `agy/_unregistered/<email>`". If the login signs in to another registered account Y, the normal path parks Y's fresh credential as unregistered, but a crash-recovered run saves it to Y. Codex login (§8.2) also moves the credential to Y.
fix: In §8.3.4 write: "Otherwise the new credential is saved by the B.5 rules (a registered email to that account's entry `agy/<id>`, keeping the later `expiry`; an unregistered one as `agy/_unregistered/<email>`), and after step 6 the command exits 65 `identity-mismatch`."

where: Appendix F: "Any change to the text increments the version, so every user accepts it again at the next `add`."; §9.3: "Until it holds the binary's current notice version … they exit 69"; §15.7 item 6: "for example after an upgrade changed the notice version … The message repeats accshift's hint."
problem: After an upgrade that bumps the notice version, `pick` and `next` exit 69 `notice-not-accepted` for every user, so routed tasks become needs-human. The only commands that write `state.notice` are `add`, which registers a new account, and `doctor --fix`, which writes it only when it recreates state.json (§6.4). No command accepts the notice for a user who already has every account registered, and the 69 hint is not defined.
fix: Add a control verb `accshift notice [--accept-notice]` (writer, under state.lock). It shows Appendix F and writes `notice = {acceptedAt, version}` on `y` or `--accept-notice`; non-interactively without the flag it exits 65 `notice-not-accepted`. List it in §10.2 and §10.4, in the §11.1 rule-8 writer list and in §6.3. Make it the `hint` of the 69 `notice-not-accepted` error (§9.3, §11.2), and have §15.7 item 6 print that command. Change Appendix F to "every user accepts it again with `accshift notice` or at the next `add`".

where: §15.7: "`--validate-only` calls only read-only commands (`version`, `list`, `status`, `pick`, `doctor --json`; §11.1 rule 8)."
problem: §15.5 says `agy models` and `--probe-models` run through `accshift exec agy --account X`, and that "`--validate-only` never asks exec for another account". §15.7 item 8 says validate-only agy model discovery "follows §15.5". So validate-only does call `exec`, which §11.1 rule 8 lists as a writer: it can take the slot lock, write the vault and update state.json.
fix: In §15.7 write: "`--validate-only` calls only read-only commands (`version`, `list`, `status`, `pick`, `doctor --json`), plus, for agy model discovery, `exec agy --account <live owner>` under the §15.5 rule." Alternatively, state that validate-only uses only cached capabilities and never runs agy discovery.

where: §15.5: "agy discovery runs only for the live slot owner: `pick agy` without `--prefer` names it, and exec takes the shared fast path for it, which writes no slot (§8.3.3). `--validate-only` … never swaps."
problem: §9.3 returns `state.agySlot.owner` only "whenever it is a usable candidate", and otherwise the first usable account. `agySlot` is null after an emptied slot or a mismatch with an unregistered email (§6.3, §8.3.3 C.3), and the owner may be limited. In those cases pick names another account, and exec swaps or writes the slot. The shared path also exists only once V-A8 has passed (§8.3.3 A). Before that, the exclusive path writes the slot when the slot copy is older than the vault snapshot (§8.3.2).
fix: In §15.5 write: "agy discovery runs only when `status agy --json` reports a non-null `agySlot.owner` and `pick agy` returns that same account; otherwise discovery is skipped with a WARNING. Such a run takes the fast path (shared once V-A8 has passed, else exclusive with no write unless the slot copy is older than the vault snapshot)." Change §15.7 item 8 to match.

where: §15.2 result table: "| 73 (`state-busy`; `next` only, since `pick` takes no lock) | transient, like the exec busy codes below |" (busy codes: "wait 60 s, re-pick, retry"); §15.3 limit branch "*) acct_outcome limit … 1) runCount=$((runCount - 1)); continue"
problem: `next` records A's limit in the same locked transaction that times out (§9.3). After a 73, nothing is recorded for A. "re-pick, retry" then calls `pick --prefer A`, which still returns A, and relaunches the task on A with the run budget refunded: a guaranteed repeat limit, looping until accountBusyWaitMinutes. The auth hook has the same problem.
fix: In §15.2 write: "73 from `next` → wait 60 s and repeat the same `next` call (same `--evidence-file`, `--exit`, `--run-started-at`, `--limited-until`), until `accountBusyWaitMinutes` of continuous busy; then treat it as the busy-limited outcome. The task is not re-run in between, and the last-run file is not truncated." Give §15.3 `acct_outcome` a separate return for this case, and add a §15.10 scenario.

where: §4.2: "A cli that `exec` cannot run on this OS is unsupported: control verbs exit 69 `unsupported-cli`"; §10.3 69: "`empty-pool` (the cli has no accounts …), `unsupported-cli` …" (no command restriction); §15.2: "(`accshift list agy --json` lists any account; a failing `list` counts as yes)"
problem: Appendix E limits 69 `empty-pool`/`unsupported-cli` to `pick` and `next`, but §4.2 and §10.3 let any control verb, including `list`, exit 69. If `list agy` exits 69 for a user with no agy accounts, or where exec cannot run agy, §15.2/§15.4 count that as "agy accounts exist". The agy runner is then routed, `pick` gives 69, and the never-unwrapped agy rule makes every agy task needs-human, where today it runs.
fix: State in §10.2/§11.2 and §10.3 that `list` and `status` always exit 0 for a known cli, with `accounts:[]` when it has no accounts or exec cannot run it. 69 `empty-pool` and `unsupported-cli` come only from `pick` and `next` (125 for exec/run). Change §4.2 to "`pick` and `next` exit 69 `unsupported-cli`". In §15.2 count `list agy` as "yes" only when it exits 0 with a non-empty `accounts`, or when it fails for a reason other than agy not being in `supportedClis`.

where: §5.2 All accounts capped: "LimitShift sleeps until then, plus its own buffer, and runs on that account (§9.3, §15)."
problem: §15.2 and Appendix E say that only a single runner (and the verifier and planner) sleeps on 75. With fallbacks, LimitShift sets `limitedUntil[R] = resetAtEpoch`, clears the current account and goes to `select_next_runner` without sleeping.
fix: In §5.2 write: "A single runner sleeps until then plus its own buffer and runs on that account; with fallbacks, LimitShift marks the runner limited until `resetAtEpoch` and tries another runner (§15.2)."

where: §8.3.4 --capture-current: "it writes only the vault and the registry." … "The notice rule of step 1 applies."
problem: The notice rule writes state.json `notice` on acceptance (§8: "On acceptance it writes `notice = {acceptedAt, version}`"), so the capture also writes state.json. §6.3 defines `agySlot.owner` as the account accshift "last put into agy's slot or last observed there". After a capture, the slot holds the newly registered account, but `agySlot` is left null or stale, so `pick agy` does not prefer the live account and the next run swaps.
fix: In §8.3.4 write: "it writes the vault and the registry, and under `state.lock` the notice (when accepted) and `state.agySlot = {owner: <new id>, store: <the store that holds it>, writtenAt}`."

where: §10.4: "| `--gh-host HOST` | `add copilot --kind gh` | string | `github.com` | the gh host, stored as `identity.host` (§8.5) |"
problem: §8.5 says "`--gh-host` (default `github.com`) is stored as `identity.host` for `token` and `gh` accounts". A.5 and §18.2 set `COPILOT_GH_HOST` from `identity.host` for `token` accounts as well. Under §10.4, `add copilot --kind token --gh-host ghe.example` is a usage error, so a GitHub Enterprise PAT can never be registered.
fix: In §10.4 change the Commands cell to "`add copilot` (`token` and `gh` kinds)".

where: §8.2: "**Add** (`accshift add codex <name> [--browser] [--import-home DIR] [--label L] [--accept-notice]`): 1. A TTY is required."
problem: §10.4 gives `add` codex `--kind home|access-token|api-key`, `--native` and `--token-stdin`. §8 says secret kinds read "one line on stdin with `--token-stdin`", and §8.2's own login says "read the new secret as at add (no-echo TTY or `--token-stdin`)". But the §8.2 add syntax omits these flags. There is no add flow for `access-token`/`api-key` (at- prefix check, vault `codex/<id>`, required `--label`, expiry tracking), and step 1 requires a TTY for every codex add.
fix: Change the §8.2 add syntax to `accshift add codex <name> [--native | --kind home|access-token|api-key] [--browser] [--import-home DIR] [--label L] [--token-stdin] [--accept-notice]`. Limit "1. A TTY is required" to the `home` kind. Add: "`access-token` / `api-key`: read the secret from a no-echo prompt or one line of `--token-stdin`; `access-token` must start with `at-` and records `expiresAt` (at most 90 days); store it as `codex/<id>`; `--label` is required (user-asserted)."

where: §8.5 gh add: "A failure exits 65 with the helper's code (`classic-pat-unsupported` or `gh-token-unavailable`)."; §10.3 65 list and Appendix E 65 row
problem: §10.3 65 and Appendix E 65 list `classic-pat-unsupported` but not `gh-token-unavailable`, which `add copilot --kind gh` exits with.
fix: Add `gh-token-unavailable` (`add copilot --kind gh`) to the §10.3 65 row and to the Appendix E 65 examples.

where: §21 M2 exit criteria: "V-W1 passes"; §22 V-W1: "… Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Break / console-close semantics with claude.exe and npm shims, daemons started by the CLI (killed with the job), junction creation without admin, the DPAPI key file over OpenSSH …"
problem: npm cmd-shim resolution and Windows junctions are M3 scope ("npm cmd-shim resolution (§12.4)", "Windows junctions + copy-back"). The Codex app-server daemon is a codex (M3) behaviour, and the DPAPI key source ships in M1. M2 cannot pass V-W1 as written, and the DPAPI part is unverified when M1 ships it.
fix: Split V-W1 across milestones. M1: the DPAPI key file over OpenSSH/S4U. M2: job-object kill tree and Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Break/console close with native `claude.exe`. M3: npm shims, junction creation and CLI-started daemons. Alternatively, move V-W1 to M3.

where: §21 M1 exit: "every §11 response validates against Appendix D; the §18.4 NFR1 and size gates pass on every runner"; §18.4: NFR1 gate includes `classify`, and "`exec` of a fake CLI for a claude `token` account … gated at 150 ms"
problem: M1's scope has no `exec`, no status file, no `classify` and no `env`; M2 delivers "exec on every OS … the status file" and "`classify claude`". M1's exit criteria require gates and schema checks for commands that do not exist until M2.
fix: In M1 write: "every §11 response of the M1 commands validates against Appendix D; the §18.4 size gate and the NFR1 gate for `version`, `list`, `pick`, `next`, `mark` and `status` pass". Move the `classify` and `exec` NFR1 gates and the classify/status-file schema checks to the M2 exit criteria.

where: §21: "Every §22 item is scheduled in exactly one milestone. V-A9 runs only if the per-directory agy mode is pursued"; M0: "… on macOS and Linux, and on Windows for the agy items"
problem: V-A9 is in no milestone, which contradicts the first sentence. V-X2 (in M0) requires Windows ("… on macOS, Linux, Windows (junctions)"), and V-C4 asks for the managed-settings paths "on each OS" (Appendix B has a Windows path). M0 runs on Windows only for the agy items, and no later milestone re-runs V-X2 or V-C4 there.
fix: Write "Every §22 item except V-A9 is scheduled in exactly one milestone; V-A9 runs only if …". In M0 write "…, and on Windows for the agy items, V-X2 and V-C4". Alternatively, schedule V-X2's Windows part in M3 next to the junction work.

where: §17.5: "Homebrew tap … | v0.2", "Scoop bucket … | v0.2", "winget … | v0.3"; §21 M7 (1.0) scope: "Homebrew/Scoop/winget"
problem: M1 publishes v0.1.0, and §17.5 brings Homebrew and Scoop at v0.2 and winget at v0.3. §21 schedules all three only in M7 (1.0).
fix: Either move "Homebrew/Scoop/winget" into the milestones that publish v0.2/v0.3, or change §17.5's "When" column to "1.0 (M7)" for those channels. State in §21 which milestone publishes v0.2 and v0.3.

where: §21 M2 scope "`token`/`native` kinds"; M6 scope "gemini (`home`/`api-key`), copilot (`token`/`gh`)"
problem: §4.2 and §8 define claude `login-slot` (experimental), gemini `native` and copilot `native`. No milestone delivers them, although §21 schedules every other kind.
